# Assessment Method v1

1. Repository evidence outranks generic benchmarks. Label evidence `observed`, `inferred`, or `unverified`.
2. Quick covers targets and immediate tests; Standard adds dependencies/integrations/data/regression; Deep adds the full reachable baseline and systemic risks.
3. A module range includes build, tests, review, integration, documentation, and applicable contingency. Totals equal included module ranges.
4. Confidence begins from evidence completeness and falls for unreachable scope, ambiguity, unfamiliar technology, missing tests, or missing Vendor decomposition.
5. AI productivity is zero unless reuse, AI-suitable work, verification coverage, and bounded ambiguity are all evidenced. Record the percentage and limitation per module.
6. Compare Vendor and AI symmetrically: overestimate, aligned, underestimate, or insufficient evidence.
7. The suggested design must reduce repeat discovery through explicit reuse boundaries, contracts, data changes, sequences, work packages, tests, rollout, rollback, and traceability.
8. Never expose secrets or unnecessary source bodies. Preserve identifiers and use the dominant case narrative language.
